Description.Name: Yang's Grand Discovery
Description.Details: Yang's voice crackles over the internal comm, out of breath and a little too excited for a man standing in a storage room full of dust. "Commander, you're gonna want to see this. I am in sub-floor 7B, in the far storage room in the aft cargo section." By the time you reach the aft cargo section, Yang and his crew have cleared out most of the junk. Crates stacked to the ceiling, tarps thick with grime, spare parts nobody's touched in decades, stacks of rusted tubing, the typical gathering of junk that builds up over time in a rear cargo area of a dropship. But all of it is shoved aside to expose a bare stretch of bulkhead, and set into that bulkhead is a wide door no one has noticed before. Yang wipes his hands on his coveralls and grins. "Wasn't looking for it. Just trying to make room for the new ammo crates. Moved a stack of scrap that's probably older than you, and there it was. Door's not on any deck plan I've ever seen." He hauls it open. Beyond it, a narrow staircase drops into darkness, the air stale and cold. The stairs seem to go on longer than they should. When you finally reach the bottom and the work lights sweep out across the space, nobody says anything for a moment. Some of it looks like a proper hangar, gantries mounted, deck plating laid, berth markings still faintly visible on the floor. But past the halfway point it just stops. Bare support ribs with no plating between them. Coiled cable that never got run. A gantry frame standing without a single panel bolted to it, tools still racked beside it like whoever was working just walked off one shift and never came back. Fifteen bays by the layout, maybe more, but less than half of them ever got finished. Whoever built this stopped partway through, and stopped for good, long before you ever took command of the Argo. "That's why it's not on any plans." Yang's voice echoes off the unfinished half of the deck. "Project like this, you don't file the paperwork till it's done. Somebody started building themselves a second hangar and ran out of money or time, or maybe both, before they ever got to call it finished." Darius crosses his arms, looking around with his usual face when his mind is running through the options. "A whole extra hangar. That's too good to just stumble upon randomly, Yang. What's the catch." Yang shrugs. "Catch is it's half a hangar dressed up as a whole one. The finished side, I could probably get that running without too much trouble. The rest needs plating, wiring, the works, same as building it new. And whoever started this never got as far as putting in a proper lift shaft big enough for a Mech. I can run elevators down here easy enough for crew and gear, that part I'm not worried about. But nothing sized for transporting a fully assembled Mech, and I'm not confident I can retrofit one into the hull with all the other changes we have done and half the systems still only partially working. Whatever gets put together down here, stays down here or comes apart to make the trip up." Sumire leans against a bulkhead, unimpressed but curious. "So we'd have two hangars, connected for everything except the one thing that matters." "Pretty much." Yang taps a bare support rib, listening to it ring. "Not gonna pretend that's convenient. But this many bays, even half finished, is a lot of bays somebody else already paid to start building." You take it in. Half a hangar, abandoned mid-build, buried inside your own ship for who knows how long. It could be worth finishing. It could also be a hole you pour money into for nothing.

Description.Name: Estimate Requirements
Description.Details: You look between Yang and the vast expanse in front of you. "Get me numbers. Costs, raw material needs, how long it would take, and what are the chances of it just being an impossible dream." Yang snaps a lazy salute. "Copy that. I'll get Farah down here, she can run the numbers on the structural and electrical side while I figure out what kind of materials and manpower we need." [Yang and Farah will report back with a full assessment of the secondary hangar in a few weeks time]
